items.body:
## Bug: cron agentTurn payload crashes with startsWith error

**Issue**: [#66283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/66283)

**Root Cause**: When a cron job with payload.kind=agentTurn fires, the qqbot gateway event handler calls parseFaceTags(event.content) where event.content is undefined. This causes:
1. parseFaceTags(undefined) crashes on .replace() call
2. Later userContent.startsWith("/") crashes on undefined

**Fix**: Accept string | undefined in parseFaceTags, return "" when input is null/undefined. Backwards compatible with existing calls.

**Testing**: pnpm test -- extensions/qqbot/src/utils/text-parsing.test.ts passed

**Files**: extensions/qqbot/src/utils/text-parsing.ts (2 lines)

```gdscript
var tex = ImageTexture.new()
```

### Describe the bug

After enabling High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS), the order add/edit screen triggers an additional AJAX request after the Heartbeat request completes. This request consistently returns a 403 response with a -1 response body due to a missing samplepermalinknonce.

User report issue here: https://wordpress.org/support/topic/hpos-order-add-edit-page-403-ajax-request-action-sample-permalink

No failing AJAX request should be triggered, or the required nonce should be present so the request succeeds.

An AJAX request is triggered after the Heartbeat request and fails with a 403 response and a -1 body because the samplepermalinknonce is missing.

1. Enable HPOS.
2. Go to WooCommerce → Orders.
3. Open an existing order (or create a new one).
4. Open the browser's Developer Tools and switch to the Network tab.
5. Click the Update (or Save) button on the order edit screen.
6. Wait for the Heartbeat AJAX request to complete.
7. Observe that another AJAX request is triggered immediately afterward and returns a 403 response with a -1 response body due to the missing samplepermalinknonce.

Runtime filter forwarding drops custom timeout and HTTP RPC size settings, so receivers fall back to defaults and may forward with inconsistent parameters.

items.body:
#### af3beda8beed365c8f045920742d74f428fe1e79 
netflix.com: v2: Webpage scrolls when adjusting volume slider (VisionOS / iPad) -- narrower fix after revert of 314097@main
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=316263
rdar://178545839

Reviewed by Abrar Rahman Protyasha and Lily Spiniolas.

The problem: on iPad and visionOS, dragging the volume slider on netflix.com
causes the page to scroll along with the gesture. Netflix's slider does not
declare touch-action: none on the element, so WebKit treats the vertical drag
as a page-scroll candidate while Netflix's react pointer handlers fire in parallel.
The original fix (310491@main, rdar://173988278) added preventDefault-on-pointerdown
plumbing to suppress this scroll, but that approach was reverted (314097@main, rdar://177895899)
because it broke synthetic-click delivery on cluesbysam.com. On iPad and
visionOS, this means the user can't drag the volume slider without scrolling
the page away from the playing video.

The fix: a quirk that adds touch-action: none on the volume slider, mirroring
the pre-existing quirk: needsGoogleMapsScrollingQuirk. the right long term fix is
for netflix to author touch-action: none themselves, since they have not,
the quirk applies the equivalent on their behalf. The quirk lives in
StyleAdjuster and matches an HTMLDivElement on netflix.com with data-uia="scrubber"
and aria-orientation="vertical". The change takes the existing touch-action
path and suppresses all browser handled gestures. Other approaches were
ruled out: a WebKit wide change to preventDefault semantics is what the previous
revert reversed, and a UA stylesheet rule on input[type=range] would affect
every site with a vertical range input.

items.title: fix(replay): fail open on replay-vision gate for scanner owners
items.body:
## Problem

Users with Replay vision access landed on the page and immediately got a "Failed to load scanners: Not found" error, leaving the product unusable. Every Replay vision API call ran through `ReplayVisionEnabledPermission`, which re-checked the `replay-vision` flag on **every request** via a live remote eval and raised `NotFound()` (404) whenever it came back falsy. The frontend gates the scene on bootstrapped client-side flags, so the page rendered, but the scanner-list request then 404'd and the frontend surfaced the toast. Because this was a per-request remote eval, a transient failure or a frontend/backend flag-gating mismatch could hard-block a team that demonstrably owned scanners — emptying the list, hiding the metrics tile, and making "Create your first scanner" unreachable (the editor sits behind the same gate).

## Changes

- `_vision_flag_enabled` now catches exceptions from the remote eval and treats them as "unknown" (logged) instead of letting them bubble — a flaky flag backend no longer hard-gates the product.
- `is_replay_vision_enabled` **fails open when the team already owns scanners**. A team with scanners has demonstrably been granted access, so a falsy/inconsistent per-request eval can't 404 the whole product out from under them. Teams with no scanners stay gated by the flag exactly as before.
- The `replay-vision-actions` sub-feature gate is unchanged in scope — it still requires its own flag (it just inherits the same exception-safety).

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent. I added API-level tests to `TestReplayScannerViewSetFeatureFlag` covering: flag-off + owned scanners → 200 (fail open), eval-raises + owned scanners → 200, and eval-raises + no scanners → 404 (gating preserved). The existing flag-off-returns-404 tests use a team with no scanners and still pass.

Local infra here lacked a working ClickHouse (the standalone binary's self-integrity check false-positives under gVisor), so I couldn't run the full DB+ClickHouse API suite locally — that runs in CI. I did verify Postgres migrations, the persons-DB setup, and exercised the real `is_replay_vision_enabled` / `is_replay_vision_actions_enabled` / `_vision_flag_enabled` functions (Django loaded, scanner-ownership queryset mocked) across all branches: flag on, flag off + owner, flag off + no owner, eval None, eval raises, and the actions gate — all pass.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Investigated from an inbox report: the symptom ("Failed to load scanners: Not found") traced to `ReplayVisionEnabledPermission` raising 404 on a per-request remote flag eval. Considered caching/local-eval vs failing open; chose failing open on scanner ownership because it directly reconciles the backend gate with the reality that the affected users own scanners, and is robust to both transient eval failures and frontend/backend flag mismatches without widening access to teams that never had it. Also made the eval exception-safe so a flaky flag backend degrades gracefully. No skills were required (no migration, serializer, or frontend-API-type changes — the change is confined to a permission/flag helper and its tests).

## Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop multi-session (split panes), **composer status-stack preview chips** (HTML / localhost artifact rows) from one session appear under another session’s composer.

Observed with two open sessions side by side:

- Left: multisession/layout chat
- Right: personal website work that produced HTML files
- **Leak:** left composer showed right-session files (`creator.html`, `ai-systems.html`, `gamer.html`, `identity-field.html`) as globe + filename + dismiss rows

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop with two sessions in a split layout (both panes mounted).
2. In session B, run a turn that produces multiple local HTML artifacts (or other previewable tool targets).
3. Keep session A focused / active as global `$activeSessionId`, or switch active session while both threads remain mounted.
4. Observe session A’s composer status stack.

## Expected Behavior

Preview artifacts are recorded and shown only for the session whose tool result produced them (`$previewStatusBySession[owningSessionId]`).

## Actual Behavior

Session B’s HTML preview chips appear under session A’s status stack.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 15.6.1
- App: Hermes Desktop / Agent **v0.18.2** (UI `# v0.18.2 (+123)`, local install around `42bd436` / upstream `ef9e0c98`)
- Surface: Electron desktop multi-session split (not CLI/TUI)

## Root Cause

**Write path uses the global active session; read path is correctly per-pane.**

### 1. Recording (wrong id)

`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx` (~309–323):

```ts
// keyed to the active session the stack reads from  ← wrong in multi-session
const activeSessionId = useStore($activeSessionId)
const currentCwd = useStore($currentCwd)
const previewTarget = view.previewTarget

useEffect(() => {
  if (isPending || !activeSessionId || !previewTarget || !isPreviewableTarget(previewTarget)) {
    return
  }
  recordPreviewArtifact(activeSessionId, previewTarget, currentCwd || '')
}, [activeSessionId, currentCwd, isPending, previewTarget])
```

- Uses global `$activeSessionId` / `$currentCwd`, not the session that owns the tool row.
- Because `activeSessionId` is in the effect deps, mounted tool rows **re-register under the new active session** when focus changes (both panes stay mounted in split view).

Blame on these lines: `42bd4368a` (status-stack preview work), under a single-session assumption that active session === stack session.

### 2. Display (correct)

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/index.tsx`:

```ts
const previews = sessionId ? (previewsBySession[sessionId] ?? []) : []
```

Composer passes per-pane `sessionId`. Isolation fails on **write**, not read.

### 3. Correct API already exists (unused here)

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-view.tsx` — `SessionView` / `useSessionView()` exposes per-tile `$runtimeId` and `$cwd` for multi-session tiles. Tool fallback bypasses that and hits primary globals.

### Why multi-session surfaces it

1. Session B produces HTML tool results → tool fallback mounts in B’s thread.
2. Global `$activeSessionId` is A (or flips to A while B stays mounted).
3. `recordPreviewArtifact` stores under A.
4. A’s status stack correctly reads A’s bucket → shows B’s files.

Also possible without split when switching active session while historical preview-bearing tool rows remount/re-effect.

## Suggested Fix

1. In tool fallback, resolve session id + cwd from **`useSessionView()`** (`$runtimeId`, `$cwd`), not `$activeSessionId` / `$currentCwd`.
2. Avoid re-keying artifacts when global focus changes (register once for the owning session when the tool completes).
3. Regression test: two mounted session tiles; tool preview in B while A is active → only B’s `$previewStatusBySession` gains the artifact.

## Related isolation debt (follow-up, not required for this repro)

`$filePreviewTabs` in `apps/desktop/src/store/preview.ts` is a **window-global** `persistentAtom` (`hermes.desktop.filePreviewTabs.v1`), not session-keyed. Right-rail file tabs can also leak across sessions. The screenshot leak matches **status-stack** `PreviewStatusRow` (globe + label + dismiss), not the rail tab strip.

## Relevant paths

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/store/preview-status.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/index.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-view.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/store/preview.ts` (related global file tabs)

## Additional Context

Screenshot available from reporter (multi-session split with website HTML chips under the non-website session’s composer). Happy to attach on request.

No code changes made by reporter beyond analysis.

<!-- You can view Contributing.MD for a detailed description of the pull request process. -->

## About The Pull Request

Removes ballast from thermomachines. That means anything to do with moving heat rather then creating it or destroying it.

I don't think ballast is something that's useful to keep around, since it functions to make cooling things harder for what amounts to no real reason.

We still have space as an infinite source of cold, it's pointless to gate it.

I'm removing all uses of two ports, cooling, efficency, work skipping, waste heat, and safeties.
This means dropping quite a lot of behavior.

There's no emag effect currently for instance, because it renabled some previously buggy behavior that was caused by ballast, which I'm nuking.

Also doing away with metal h2 upgrades to the thing, because even though I like the idea, it has no purpose as of now.

Removing ballast has made a lot of the logic and checks that were done in process_atmos pointless, so they can go too.
I'm keeping the barebones behavior of how power consumption works, because I like it.

Efficency is going because it was almost always like 80% without ballast, and I didn't think it was something worth having.
Cooling as a concept can go interestingly enough, because there's no difference between heating and cooling, just the temperature we're targeting.

I've also restored heat capacity to its old value, since the current one was bumped up a bit to compensate for other aspects of the machine that limit heating speed.

I think that's about it? I'm also removing failure states, because they too were linked to ballast
Cleaned up the examine a bit, and removed some redundant code 

Oh, and I'm removing the redundant icon states and gags entries, since well, they aren't used anymore. 
Also removed some from the js file

Fixes https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/issues/66440
Someone forgot to remove the old multitool act proc. Broke behavior. I've fixed it

## Why It's Good For The Game

I was a bit worried about this feature initially, but let it be because it wasn't causing any harm.
Ghil has been unable to go in the direction he wanted to with heat management, because it unlike this change was something I am not down with.

Because of that, thermomachines have been in this kinda annoying state, where they're easy to use in some ways, but have a lot of extra stuff you need to manage.
Because we're finally starting to work on making atmos more accessible, it needs to go.

Oh and btw, I've split my work into a few different commits, so you can look at what I removed separate from the repath. FYI.

If you're just here to mald about ballast, piss off. I am not interested in playing host to you.
